title: s$^3$: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL
summary: Cooperative reinforcement learning trained language-model agent teams to learn when to solve subtasks independently and when to share information. On held-out information-aggregation and exploration tasks, the authors report improved coordination when testing teams at twice the training size, reduced repeated work and gains over best-of-N under matched budgets. Evidence is limited to the paper’s constructed tasks and small open models.
ai_technology: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning lets language-model agents learn when to work independently and share information.
organization: University of California, Berkeley; University of Washington

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: Matched-budget controls, six-seed held-out evaluations and ablations were reported on constructed coordination and exploration tasks.
evidence.unknown: Small-model and synthetic-task evaluation does not establish general real-world agent performance.
